input.summary: Someone used Jordan Doe's (jdoe@example.com) identity against the payments-prod clusters on all three clouds: EKS from 14:02Z, GKE from 14:38Z and AKS from 15:11Z on 2026-10-14. Every request came from 198.51.100.23, a known-bad bulletproof-hosting VPS (NIGHTOWL-HOSTING, NL, tagged for running an open Docker registry and brute-forcing k8s APIs). Jordan is on PTO 2026-10-12..19 and normally uses macOS, but this client was kubectl on linux/amd64. On each cluster the actor ran the same playbook. They checked their permissions and listed namespaces, then tried kube-system secrets and a kube-system job, both denied. They read payments/payments-db-credentials, created a privileged pod (hostPID/hostNetwork, host / mounted) and exec'd nsenter into the node. Next they used the argocd-application-controller service account token (cluster-admin) from their own external IP, although that account only runs in-cluster. With it they created ClusterRoleBinding jdoe-break-glass, giving jdoe cluster-admin. They then set up persistence: a kube-system DaemonSet kube-metrics-agent and a CronJob node-cert-rotate that pull images from the attacker's registry 198.51.100.23:5000, plus NodePort service metrics-agent-np on port 30080. Last came the alerted cluster-wide list of all secrets. Scope: all three clusters, payments DB credentials and all cluster secrets exposed, and full node and cluster-admin compromise.

Last came the alerted cluster-wide list of all secrets. Scope: all three clusters, payments DB credentials and all cluster secrets exposed, and full node and cluster-admin compromise.
